info.title: Pipe Solar API
info.description: Every call sends a company key, made by an owner or admin in Settings → API Keys, as Authorization: Bearer psk_…. Call from a server, never from a web page. Documentation: https://developers.pipe.solar

customFields.description: The company's own fields on the project (Settings → Company fields), by the field's name: text, a number, a YYYY-MM-DD date, a choice, or true and false. A field with no value is left out.

get.description: Answers the key's name and the company it belongs to. Use it to prove a key works before you build on it.

401.description: The key is missing, wrong or revoked.

429.description: More than 100 calls in a minute from this key; wait the seconds `Retry-After` names.

get.description: Your company's projects, solar and HI, newest change first, a page at a time. Keep the newest `updatedAt` you read and send it as `updatedSince` next time to read only what changed. An installer's key lists every project it builds, its dealers' included.

200.description: `data` holds the page's projects, the core of each; `next` is the cursor for the next page, or null at the end.

400.description: The request is not valid; the message says what to change.

401.description: The key is missing, wrong or revoked.

429.description: More than 100 calls in a minute from this key; wait the seconds `Retry-After` names.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Rows in a page, 1 to 100. 50 when absent.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next` of the page before, URL-encoded, with the same other fields. Absent for the first page.

parameters.name: updatedSince
parameters.description: Only rows changed after this time, ISO 8601 (2026-10-01T00:00:00Z).

get.description: One project in full: the customer, the people, the contract, the financing, the milestones and the files. A solar project carries `system` and an HI project `products`; `productLine` says which, and the other is null. `{id}` is Pipe's id, or the reference your system holds from the old app: the 10-character UID of the customer or the project, or the old app's own id of either. A project also answers to its lead's id.

401.description: The key is missing, wrong or revoked.

404.description: No record with this id is yours.

429.description: More than 100 calls in a minute from this key; wait the seconds `Retry-After` names.

get.description: The stages a project can move to, each ladder in its own order: solar's, then HI's. Key your system on `id`, never on the name: renaming a stage in Settings keeps its id, so an automation that sends `stageId` keeps working. Where your company keeps no ladder of its own for a product line, its projects use Pipe's standard one, so the same id can appear under both lines. Only the installer's key reads the ladders.

200.description: `data` holds the stages, in ladder order; `position` counts from 1 within each product line.

400.description: The request is not valid; the message says what to change.

401.description: The key is missing, wrong or revoked.

403.description: A dealer's key: only the installer's key reads its ladders.

429.description: More than 100 calls in a minute from this key; wait the seconds `Retry-After` names.

post.description: Moves the project into a stage of its own ladder, as the Move button does: the stage's checklists, alerts and messages follow. Name the stage by `stageId` (from GET /v1/stages, or a project's `stage.id`), which a rename never breaks, or by its name as `stage`; send one, not both. The stage travels in the body, never in the address, so a name needs no encoding. The stage it is already in changes nothing. Only the installer's key moves a project. `{id}` is Pipe's id, or the reference your system holds from the old app: the 10-character UID of the customer or the project, or the old app's own id of either. A project also answers to its lead's id.

200.description: `changed` says whether it moved; `stage` is the stage's name and `stageId` its id.

400.description: No such stage on this project's ladder, both or neither of `stageId` and `stage`, or not the installer's key; a wrong name lists the ladder's stages.

401.description: The key is missing, wrong or revoked.

404.description: No record with this id is yours.

parameters.description: `{id}` is Pipe's id, or the reference your system holds from the old app: the 10-character UID of the customer or the project, or the old app's own id of either. A project also answers to its lead's id.

stageId.description: The stage's id, as GET /v1/stages lists it. Preferred: a rename keeps it.

stage.description: The stage's name, as the ladder shows it, when you send no `stageId`. Case does not matter.

post.description: Copies each file from its address into the project's folder, where the record shows it. Send 1 to 10 at a time. Each address must be public https (no IP address, no private name, no password in it), open the file without signing in, and hold a document, picture, audio or video of 100 MB or less; Pipe keeps its own copy. Sending the same address to the same folder again adds nothing. Only the installer's key adds files. `{id}` is Pipe's id, or the reference your system holds from the old app: the 10-character UID of the customer or the project, or the old app's own id of either. A project also answers to its lead's id.

200.description: Every address was already in this folder; nothing was added.

201.description: `files` lists each file with its id; `added` is false for an address this folder already holds, so a retry adds nothing twice.

files.description: A list of { url, name }: a public https address, and the name to show (the address's own when absent).

post.description: Sends one homeowner to Pipe as a lead in the key's company. Send the same externalId again and the answer is the lead it already made, so a retried call makes no duplicate.

200.description: The externalId was sent before; the answer is that lead.

400.description: The body is not valid; the error says why.

401.description: The key is missing, wrong or revoked.

address.description: line1, city, state and postalCode; line2 and country are optional. state is a US state or Canadian province (TX, ON, or the name); country is US or CA, read from the state when absent.

salesRepEmail.description: An active member of the company. Any other email leaves the rep empty and is listed under unassigned.

setterEmail.description: The same rule as salesRepEmail, for the setter.

notes.description: Saved on the lead and posted to its activity.

externalId.description: Your system's id, at most 128 characters.

get.description: One lead: the customer, the address, the status, the source, the people and its files by folder. `proposal` is the option the lead leads with (the one the customer chose, else the newest): its system, price, financing and adders, so a lead can be followed before it sells. `project` names the project once the customer bought. `{id}` is Pipe's id, or the reference your system holds from the old app: the 10-character UID of the customer or the project, or the old app's own id of either. A project also answers to its lead's id.

401.description: The key is missing, wrong or revoked.

patch.description: Changes the customer's details, as the record's edit dialogs do, and the sales rep and setter, as the record's Members window does. An absent field is kept, and null clears an optional one, so a lead read here can be sent back as it is; the answer is the lead as it now reads. A new rep or setter must be an active member of the lead's company, or the call is refused and changes nothing. A rep taken off the lead loses it unless a share still reaches it. `{id}` is Pipe's id, or the reference your system holds from the old app: the 10-character UID of the customer or the project, or the old app's own id of either. A project also answers to its lead's id.

notes.description: The lead's notes; also posted to its activity.

address.description: line1, city, state and postalCode together; line2 and country are optional. state is a US state or Canadian province (TX, ON, or the name); country is US or CA, read from the state when absent.

coBorrower.description: firstName, lastName, email, phone; an empty text clears that field.

salesRepEmail.description: The sales rep, by their sign-in email: an active member of the lead's company. Any other email is refused with `invalid`, naming it. An empty text or null takes the rep off the lead.

setterEmail.description: The same rule as salesRepEmail, for the setter.

get.description: The lead's Activity tab, newest first, a page at a time: notes, status and stage changes, files, and the rest. `createdAt` is when the row was first written, and `reference` the old id of a row written before the move to this API (null for a newer row). The pages run in the order Pipe recorded the rows, and rows written before the move were recorded together, so sort by `createdAt` when the exact order matters. `internal` marks a note only the company's admins see. `author` is the writer's name and `authorId` their id, the same id the activity webhook sends; both are null for a row the app wrote, and `authorId` is null for the homeowner. `{id}` is Pipe's id, or the reference your system holds from the old app: the 10-character UID of the customer or the project, or the old app's own id of either. A project also answers to its lead's id.
